Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNodeSetOperations` checks the evaluation of the XPath expression `$array > 0` and expects a Boolean.TRUE result. The current bug report states that binary operators involving node-sets behave incorrectly, especially when comparing node-sets to numbers, as per the XPath specification: when comparing node-set operands, the comparison should be true if there exists any node in the first node-set and any node in the second node-set such that the comparison on their string-values is true.

The failure likely comes from the binary operation logic in the implementation of these operators like `CoreOperationEqual` or other core operation classes which handle comparisons. The snippet of `CoreOperationEqual.computeValue` simply returns the result of the `equal()` method applied to the operands, but the core of the issue lies in how binary operators process node-set operands before comparison.

The recent bug reports do not seem relevant to node-set comparison logic; they concern binary compatibility, missing field setting, and string trimming issues.

Therefore, the root cause is that the binary operation implementation does not correctly handle node-sets per the XPath specification, probably failing to iterate and compare nodes' string values as required when either or both operands are node-sets.

To pinpoint and fix the error, we should examine the binary operations handling code, especially the relevant CoreOperation subclasses (`CoreOperationEqual`, `CoreOperationLessThanOrEqual`, etc.) and their methods that perform the comparison logic on node-set operands. The code likely misses the special treatment for node-sets where it must check for any pair of nodes satisfying the comparison rather than direct object comparison.

This explains the failing test case where `$array > 0` involving a node-set and a number does not yield the correct Boolean result.

Next, I will check the `equal` method or equivalent methods that implement comparison to see if they handle node-sets according to the spec.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
